questions.text: Scientific planning of transportation system and mass transit facilities in cities should be based on
questions.expl: Origin and destination (O-D) survey data forms the essential basis for scientific transportation and mass transit planning, since it reveals actual travel demand patterns.

questions.text: Equivalent factor of passenger car unit (PCU) for auto rickshaw as per IRC is
questions.expl: IRC assigns an auto-rickshaw a passenger car unit (PCU) equivalent value of about 0.5, reflecting its smaller size and impact on traffic flow relative to a car.

questions.text: With increase in speed of the traffic stream, the minimum spacing of vehicles
options: First decreases and then increases after reaching a minimum value at optimum speed
First increases and then decreases after reaching a maximum value at optimum speed
questions.expl: As traffic stream speed increases, drivers require greater stopping/reaction distance, so the minimum spacing between vehicles also increases.

questions.text: The diagram which show the optimum path vehicles and pedestrians involved in the accidents is known as
questions.expl: A collision diagram graphically depicts the paths and movements of vehicles/pedestrians involved in accidents at a location, helping identify accident patterns.

questions.text: In cement concrete roads, the repair work of cracks should be done just at the end of
questions.expl: Crack repair in cement concrete roads is best carried out at the end of the rainy season, once moisture-related movement has stabilized and before further seasonal stress cycles.

questions.text: Patching should be done just
questions.expl: Patching of pavement defects should be completed before the rainy season, to prevent water infiltration into damaged areas during rains.

questions.text: 'Weaving' is
questions.expl: Weaving describes the combined traffic maneuver in which vehicles merge into a stream, travel alongside other traffic, and then diverge - hence the full combined process.

questions.text: An instrument used to study 'Spot Speeds' in traffic engineering is
questions.expl: An enoscope is a traditional optical device used to measure the spot speed of vehicles passing a fixed point on the road.

questions.text: An advantage of 'one way traffic' system is
options: reduced number of points of conflicts
questions.expl: One-way traffic systems eliminate opposing traffic movements at intersections, significantly reducing the number of vehicle conflict points.

questions.text: The number of vehicles moving in a specified direction on a roadway that pass a given point during specified unit of time, is called
questions.expl: Traffic volume is defined as the number of vehicles passing a given point on the roadway in a specified direction during a specified unit of time.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a regulatory sign?
questions.expl: 'School zone' is a warning/cautionary sign alerting drivers to nearby children, not a regulatory sign like the prohibition signs listed alongside it.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a warning sign?
questions.expl: 'No Entry' is a regulatory (prohibitory) sign that legally bars vehicles from entering, unlike the other options which merely warn of upcoming road features.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a informatory sign?
questions.expl: 'Speed limit' is a regulatory sign that legally restricts vehicle speed, not merely an informatory sign like road names or destination signs.

questions.text: If the stopping distance and average length of a vehicle are 18m and 6m respectively, then the theoretical maximum capacity (vehicles per hour) of a traffic lane at a speed of 10m/sec is
questions.expl: Capacity = (speed × 3600)/(stopping distance + vehicle length) = (10×3600)/(18+6) = 36000/24 = 1500 vehicles per hour.

questions.text: Speed regulations on roads are decided on the basis of
questions.expl: Speed regulations (speed limits) are typically set based on the 85th percentile speed from the cumulative frequency distribution of observed vehicle speeds.
